issues.description: PKGBUILD is Arch Linux-specific (pacman-based). Alpine uses apk/PKG build files. CLI help text references 'CachyOS PKGBUILD dir'.

locations.type: systemd service references in CLI help text
locations.description: CLI help text references systemd .service unit names. Alpine uses OpenRC runlevels/scripts. These are user-facing doc strings; actual service files are elsewhere in repo but CLI must be updated to mention OpenRC equivalents.
Help text references 'initramfs' and 'initcpio' (Arch/Dracut terminology). Alpine uses a different initramfs mechanism (mkimage/initramfs).

issues.description: CLI prints `mkinitcpio -P` (Arch-specific initramfs rebuild tool). Alpine uses a different initramfs mechanism.

locations.type: Arch install instructions in error message
locations.description: Error message for cu health-test shows PKGBUILD/makepkg + pacman install instructions for umr and RADV. Alpine users need apk-based install instructions.

issues.description: The entire boot() and install() functions write a systemd .service unit file with systemd directives (Type=oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes, WantedBy=multi-user.target, After=multi-user.target). Alpine uses OpenRC runscripts instead. The UNIT_NAME constant references 'aputune-cores.service' and UNIT_PATH is '/etc/systemd/system/'. All systemctl invocations (daemon-reload, enable, disable, reboot) are systemd-specific.

acpi_install() and acpi_revert() are entirely Arch-specific: references to /etc/mkinitcpio.conf, parsing HOOKS=(...) syntax, injecting 'acpi_override' hook, running 'mkinitcpio -P'. ACPI override directory is /etc/initcpio/. These functions are unusable on Alpine which uses mkimage / different initramfs mechanisms. The constants MKINITCPIO_CONF, ACPI_OVERRIDE_DIR, ACPI_BACKUP_DIR are Arch paths.

set_warm_reboot() sets /sys/kernel/reboot/mode (this path is kernel-level and works on all Linux including Alpine), but the actual reboot uses systemctl reboot which is systemd-specific. On Alpine, a simple 'reboot' command or /sys/class/smi/reboot would be needed. The warm reboot mode itself (writing to /sys/kernel/reboot/mode) should be fine on Alpine.
